**Analysis:**
- Test image: Close-up of a soybean stem at a node showing **gray/white fluffy cottony growth** concentrated right at the node junction
- Surrounding leaves are heavily yellowed (fallen to background)
- The green stem with gray mycelial growth at the node is characteristic

**Key comparisons:**
- **White_Mold** ✓: "fluffy, white growth on soybean stems with gray to white lesions at nodes" — matches exactly. Reference shows similar cottony white/gray mycelial growth on stems at nodes.
- **Powdery_Mildew** ✗: Gray powdery coating on leaf surfaces, not concentrated at stem nodes
- **Downy_mildew** ✗: Gray growth on leaf undersides
- **Charcoal_Rot** ✗: Bleached stems with tiny black specks, no fluffy mycelium
- **Rhizoctonia** ✗: Root/hypocotyl rot, reddish-brown lesions
- **Diaporthe** ✗: Linear rows of black pycnidia on stems

The gray fluffy/cottony mycelial growth at the node on a green stem is the hallmark sign of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).
